name: Eutychus
overview: Eutychus was a young male mentioned in the New Testament who is notably remembered for falling from a third-floor window during a gathering. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details. His brief mention highlights a significant incident during an early Christian meeting.
namesAndTitles: The name Eutychus appears once in Scripture without a provided meaning or special significance. It is presented simply as a proper name in the book of Acts.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Eutychus beyond the incident in which he is involved. There are no listed connections to other individuals or family members.
scriptureSignificance: Eutychus is significant for the event in Acts 20:9 where he fell from a third-story window, an incident that underscores the dangers faced during early Christian gatherings and the care of the apostolic community. His story serves as a reminder of God's power to preserve and restore, as the narrative implies his recovery following the fall. Though briefly mentioned, Eutychus' experience contributes to the broader testimony of the early church's life and ministry.
